label: Chapter 3: How it lost the money

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. There's a "but" coming.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There is. And it's a heavy one.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: This part is not funny.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Understood.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1566 and 1567, religious riots and unrest in the Low Countries brought Spanish troops to the region.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Antwerp was a rich trading city in a Catholic king's empire.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And then?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In November 1576, Spanish troops sacked the city.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's called the Spanish Fury. About 6,000 people were killed, and about 800 houses were burned.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The new town hall was gutted by the fire.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's brutal.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It is. And it wasn't the end. In 1585, after a long siege, Alessandro Farnese, the Duke of Parma, took the city for Spain.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Many Protestants were forced to leave.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And they took their skills with them.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And their money. Amsterdam became the new trading center.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And then something worse?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1648, the Treaty of Münster closed the Scheldt to shipping.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The river that had made Antwerp rich was shut at the mouth.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So a port with no ships.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: By 1800 the population had fallen below 40,000.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That was the low point.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: How did it recover?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Slowly. Napoleon eased the restrictions and paid for new docks, starting with the Bonaparte Dock in 1811.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The restriction on the river ended in 1863.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And in 1859, the old 16th-century walls came down, to make room for broad avenues.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So the city grew back.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It did. A new stock exchange in 1872.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A grand central station, finished in 1905.
